newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money unchanged in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money unchanged in liquid market.

text.p: * Central Bank maintains overnight borrowing at 10.5 pct
Manila overnight money was unchanged at an average of 10.5625 percent on Tuesday amid the high liquidity in the market, dealers said.
"The floor on interest rates will still be the Central Bank's rates," a dealer from a big bank said.
Banks were just investing their money in the Central Bank's special series T-bills and Treasury notes, they said.
Banks had been awash with money because they have been shying away from term reverse repos which had been charged a 20 percent tax.
Done rates ranged from 11.00 to 10.53125 percent, with 34 lenders and 25 borrowers. Market volume was higher at 21.098 billion from 19.581 billion pesos.
Meanwhile, banks continued to place their money in short-term bills due to the high liquidity in the market.
"They're playing it safe," a dealer said, in case interest rates start to move up. Banks feel interest rates have fallen too fast.
Banks were quoting bid rates of 10.65 to 10.70 percent for three-month bills, a Reuter poll of eight financial institutions showed.
